questions.question: TGI (Text Generation Inference) entered maintenance mode on what date, and what does that mean for new projects?
options: January 1, 2026; means no new features but security patches continue
December 11, 2025; means only bug fixes, making it a risky long-term bet — prefer vLLM or SGLang
March 2026; means HuggingFace deprecated it in favor of their new serving stack
TGI is not in maintenance mode; it is the recommended default in 2026
questions.explanation: TGI entered maintenance mode on December 11, 2025 — only bug fixes going forward. This biases new projects toward vLLM or SGLang. TGI has historically had top observability and HF-ecosystem integration, but its maintenance status makes it a risky long-term foundation.

questions.question: Which self-hosted engine is the only option when running on CPU-only hardware?
options: Ollama
vLLM
llama.cpp
SGLang
questions.explanation: CPU-only hardware forces llama.cpp — it is the only engine of the five that runs without a GPU. vLLM, SGLang, and TRT-LLM all require NVIDIA GPUs. Ollama wraps llama.cpp but adds overhead.

questions.question: What throughput penalty does Ollama carry versus llama.cpp under production-like load?
options: Ollama is faster due to better HTTP connection pooling
~5% slower under any load
15-30% slower; 3x throughput gap under production-like load
Identical to llama.cpp — Ollama is just a wrapper with no overhead
questions.explanation: Ollama is 15-30% slower than llama.cpp due to Go + CGo + HTTP serialization overhead. Under production-like load (concurrent requests), the gap widens to approximately 3x throughput. Ollama is for developer laptops, not serving.

questions.question: Why can AMD GPUs only use vLLM and not TRT-LLM for self-hosted serving?
options: AMD does not support the ROCm driver version required by TRT-LLM
TRT-LLM is an NVIDIA-only closed stack and does not compile for AMD hardware
AMD GPUs lack NVLink, which TRT-LLM requires for KV cache transfer
TRT-LLM's NVFP4 format is specific to Blackwell Tensor Cores not found in AMD
questions.explanation: TRT-LLM is a closed NVIDIA stack — it uses NVIDIA-specific primitives (CUDA, NVLink, TensorRT kernels) and does not build for AMD hardware. vLLM has ROCm support and is the only option for AMD GPU self-hosted serving.

questions.question: What is the recommended dev/staging/prod pipeline for self-hosted serving in 2026?
options: Dev: vLLM local, Staging: TGI, Prod: TRT-LLM
Dev: Ollama, Staging: llama.cpp, Prod: vLLM or SGLang — same GGUF/HF weights throughout
Dev: HuggingFace transformers, Staging: TGI, Prod: vLLM
Dev, Staging, and Prod all use the same engine for consistency
questions.explanation: The 2026 pipeline pattern: dev = Ollama (one-command install), staging = llama.cpp (CPU-accurate reference), prod = vLLM or SGLang. The key insight is using the same GGUF or HF weights throughout — format compatibility enables the pipeline.

questions.question: When should SGLang be chosen over vLLM as the production serving engine?
options: When running on Blackwell hardware with NVFP4 weights
For agentic multi-turn workloads and prefix-heavy RAG where shared prefix reuse is high
When the model is under 8B parameters
When AMD GPU hardware is required
questions.explanation: SGLang wins for agentic multi-turn workloads and prefix-heavy RAG — its RadixAttention and cache-aware scheduling deliver 29-640% throughput improvements over vLLM on these patterns. vLLM is the general-purpose default for workloads without strong prefix locality.
